shared_contract.authority_status: Wire/event names below are now explicit normative offline construction targets. This document grants no enrolled production identity, new runtime action or source mutation.

wire_and_delegation.encoding: Each NEW signed envelope (schema-2 purpose grant and the three new wire messages) has EXACT keys body,signature. body has the exact field set for its kind below; signature is 128 lowercase hex characters. Canonical body is AdmissionAuthority.canonical: sorted compact ASCII JSON, ensure_ascii=True, allow_nan=False, no newline. Strict byte parser rejects duplicate keys at every depth, nonfinite numbers, unknown/missing fields, noncanonical encodings and oversized inputs before signature validation. Explicit NUL in each signature prefix is one 0x00 byte. Never reuse supervisor process-response newline encoding. Existing base ROOT_GRANT/v1 and signed V2 disclosure-policy envelopes keep their original byte/signature format; never rewrap or reinterpret them.
wire_and_delegation.type_rules: schema/purpose_version/ordinal/epochs/lengths are exact int (never bool). schema=1 and purpose_version=1 for all three wire bodies; ordinal=0 for this first slice. Digests are lowercase SHA-256 hex. IDs nonempty bounded strings <=128 UTF-8 bytes except existing BINDINGS <=512; reject NUL. Timestamps timezone-aware ISO-8601. mcp_id is a <=128-byte string or exact int 0..2^53-1, preserving JSON type. domain_tag must equal the concrete authority domain. No arbitrary error text. Lengths are nonnegative within bounds; epochs/revisions positive. Claim/ACK issued_at cannot be in the future and effective expiry is the minimum applicable purpose/grant/policy/window expiry.

claim_request.constraints: tool_name=read_artifact; transformation=READ_APPROVED_ARTIFACT; arguments has EXACT field artifact_id and its value equals artifact_id. arguments_sha256 hashes its canonical bytes. All context, tool/source/envelope/version, expected artifact digest, limits and parent identity match the signed purpose grant. Parent supplies request/operation/ordinal; worker supplies only untrusted artifact_id/mcp_id. operation_id = digest({root_allocation_id, operation_kind:PARENT_TOOL_READ, ordinal:0}); request_id is correlation only, never uniqueness authority. Bounded first canonical allocation binding prevents grant renewal from resetting this operation.

observation.constraints: Same signer and parent identity/boot/process as accepted request, exact claim seq/hash and canonical signed request-envelope digest. RETURNED has error_code=null and non-null raw/result fields. ERROR has one fixed code READ_FAILED/INPUT_MISMATCH/LIMIT_EXCEEDED/INVALID_UTF8 and all byte/digest/length fields null; UNKNOWN has error_code=UNKNOWN and all byte fields null. A RETURNED record contains exact actual raw bytes and exact serialized response, never a caller-selected path/reference. effect_started_at lies within accepted claim start window; observed_at >= effect_started_at. Missing evidence never means RETURNED.

commit_ack.constraints: phase=CLAIM or OUTCOME; status=COMMITTED only. CLAIM has observation_sha256/raw/result hashes and lengths null; accepted_kind=PARENT_TOOL_READ_CLAIMED and accepted seq/hash equal claim seq/hash. OUTCOME binds the exact signed observation envelope digest and its PARENT_TOOL_OBSERVATION_RECORDED row plus original claim; only verified RETURNED yields a result-release ACK. commit_head_hash=accepted_row_hash (the head at that append); verified_head_hash is an actually read verified descendant head, not necessarily unchanged head. Echo exact parent/operation/ordinal/context/request. ACK proves accepted-row binding, not fresh execution/egress authority.

root_purpose_grant.purpose_entries: Exactly one entry for each of PARENT_TOOL_CLAIM_REQUEST, PARENT_TOOL_OBSERVATION and PARENT_TOOL_COMMIT_ACK, purpose_version=1; no wildcard/generic observer role. Root grant signature is verified against independently enrolled FrozenTrust.roots.
root_purpose_grant.base_join: parent_grant_id/digest resolves the existing schema-1 grant with its original verification rules. Schema-2 grant issuer equals that base grant root issuer; bindings and base admission/policy match exactly. Distinct grant ID, no duplicate/ambiguous trust entries. Root-signed v2 purpose grant cannot expand expiry, scope, parent root allocation, frame allowance or signed V2 policy/rule. policy_signer_id resolves an independently enrolled FrozenTrust root used by the existing signed V2 policy verifier. Raw policy bytes are immutable explicit inputs pinned by signed_v2_manifest_sha256; no file/key discovery.
root_purpose_grant.parent_signer: Claim and observation entries identify the same independently enrolled existing protected supervisor public key; public-key digest must equal parent_identity_sha256 from the grant and trusted parent binding. Signature of a boot/launch response alone does not establish this enrollment/purpose.
root_purpose_grant.ack_signer: ACK entry names the existing base grant delegate_id, independently enrolled in FrozenTrust.identities, and explicitly grants only this ACK purpose. It must differ from parent signer and root issuer. It runs in the protected canonical-authority/root-client boundary; private key stays out of worker, argv/env/queue and MCP. The grant root issuer signs the delegation offline only. No production mapping or private-key availability is claimed; absent matching explicit purpose => deny.
root_purpose_grant.limits: max_operations=1 across this inherited root_allocation_id for PARENT_TOOL_READ; max_raw_bytes<=16384, max_result_bytes<=131072, and both <= applicable signed derivative policy bounds. start_window_seconds is exact int 1..30. All purpose expiries <= purpose-grant expiry <= base grant expiry and policy expiry. All source/scope/version/policy/rule bindings exact. No default positive purpose grants.
root_purpose_grant.legacy_denial: Do not broaden existing _signature/_grant/issue/append_signed or legacy send settlement to accept schema-2 tool evidence implicitly. Dedicated versioned APIs verify this new purpose. V1 root grants/CURRENT/SEND_EVIDENCE and legacy delegate/reconciler labels alone grant no tool/ACK purpose.

canonical_retention_and_lifecycle.store_evidence: kernel/ledger.py:86-106,300-316,371-423 supports JSON event payload and accepted-row/chain readback. kernel/ledger_sqlite.py:61,109-145,154-178 uses synchronous=FULL, transactional head check/insert and JSON TEXT readback. No inspected application row-size cap precludes the conservative bound; durable capacity/crash behavior must be tested later, not claimed now.

claim_event.constraints: schema=1; retained signed request/base grant/tool grant envelope bytes are canonical strict encodings. Verify request purpose, signatures, parent scope, all current bindings and existing allocation state before append_if_head. Revalidate entire snapshot on CAS conflict. Duplicate operation, same allocation regrant or ambiguous previous claim denies before read. No future own seq/hash field in payload. base_grant_b64 retains the existing v1 signed format, not a new wire envelope; tool_grant_b64 retains the new v2 envelope. Canonicalize only the formats their existing/new signature contracts prescribe.

outcome_event.constraints: One immutable outcome per claim; observation_b64 contains the full signed observation including canonical base64 raw/result bytes. Validate signatures and exact historical claim from the concrete Ledger, never caller rows. No auto-upgrade from ERROR/UNKNOWN or conflicting duplicate append. Late recording of historical claim outcome is permitted after revocation only under captured claim-time purpose proof; it cannot grant new use.

bounds_and_readback: Application checks canonical JSON event payload <=262144 bytes before append; wire envelope <=196608 bytes, claim request <=32768 bytes, each root-grant envelope <=16384 bytes. Bounds include base64/signature overhead; if total exceeds bound, refuse before append/read or release. Canonical standard padded base64 only: validate encoded length before decoding and require re-encoding equality.

First-slice actual raw input <=16384 bytes. Exact result envelope <=131072 bytes; lower signed policy/grant/mediator limits prevail. No external CAS or arbitrary file reference permitted. Oversize/error cannot release content or fall back to a sidecar. Existing Ledger append/rejection behavior is retained.

Hash raw read bytes once, require expected SHA and UTF-8 validity; input set is exactly the grant/rule-bound artifact. The result is the complete existing MCP JSON-RPC response: inner result json.dumps({artifact_id,text,sha256}, sort_keys=True) with existing default spacing/ASCII escaping; outer {jsonrpc:"2.0",id:mcp_id,result:{content:[{type:"text",text:inner}]}} uses sort_keys=True,separators=(",",":"),ensure_ascii=True, then exactly one LF. Verify raw digest/length, decoded text and recomputed result bytes independently. A raw hash, envelope hash and full provider-frame hash are different identities.

Root authority rereads exact accepted seq from its OWN concrete Ledger, verifies chain/domain/row hash, claim/outcome signatures and all retained bytes. ACK producer cannot accept caller-provided Ledger rows, digest dictionaries or positive callbacks. It signs only after that readback. ACK verifier on canonical side independently repeats readback; fake-but-signed ACK for absent/different row fails.

Parent-side ACK signature validation authenticates the designated technical commit attestation; it is not an independent Ledger reader. Canonical append evidence comes from the concrete issuer readback and is rechecked by the eventual canonical consumer. Parent verifies expected phase/context/operation/nonce/row/byte digests before release. If issuer readback or protected signer/channel cannot be established, no ACK/content release. A signed or fsynced queue file alone never qualifies.

No broad capacity claim: if bounded inline append/readback is unsupported in the selected store, stop with exact kernel/ledger.py/kernel/ledger_sqlite.py primitive evidence and request owner scope; do not introduce CAS/sidecar or change those immutable files in the first slice.
canonical_retention_and_lifecycle.ordering: Validate current base/purpose trust, admission, canonical policy plus signed V2 rule/source/scope; CAS claim; committed claim readback and CLAIM ACK; exactly one parent read for that live pending parent boot/process/operation; compute/retain signed observation; CAS outcome; readback and OUTCOME ACK; release exact stored result only. ACK never independently starts a tool. Duplicate ACK is ignored; no awaiting-call recreation after crash. All mutations remain on one canonical Ledger.
canonical_retention_and_lifecycle.currentness: Revocation/expiry/supersession/source mismatch checked at claim and at every fresh consumption/result replay. Existing base root-grant/admission/policy revocation invalidates the derived purpose; matching v2-grant revocation or malformed relevant canonical revocation also denies. Claim-first may record historical completion, but revocation-first permits zero read and later invalidation always denies new disclosure. Historical receipt checks use signed proofs retained with the accepted claim; expiry is not ignored for fresh use. Outcome ACK/result replay requires live/current bound context; otherwise preserve historical row without release.
canonical_retention_and_lifecycle.crash_and_replay: Before successful claim: no read, fresh validation may retry only within an issued attempt budget. After claim: no reread, reset, new-ordinal/session/request-ID reuse or automatic retry, even when no output row exists. Unsettled is non-consumable UNKNOWN-equivalent; it needs no forged parent UNKNOWN signature. Explicit signed UNKNOWN/ERROR is terminal. If exact RETURNED outcome is already committed, requery may produce a fresh purpose-authenticated ACK for the SAME operation/phase and replay only its stored bytes under current scope; never reread source. Lost send ACK uses existing send reconciliation, never resend.
canonical_retention_and_lifecycle.future_consumption: Separate fence scope must bind sorted witness row/claim digests, raw/result identities and actual complete provider frame/route/root-allocation ordinal in the same existing ADMISSION_SEND_CLAIMED CAS after currentness re-evaluation. One witness to one explicitly allocated provider frame by default. No hash-only permission, exact-allowlist auto-expansion or implicit repeated transcript reuse. Readback object/ACK is not a send lease.

proposed_APIs: AdmissionAuthority(..., tool_policy_manifests: tuple[bytes,...]=()): immutable explicit signed V2 policy bytes; empty defaults deny this purpose. No enrollment/file reads or discovery; verify with enrolled root identity and purpose-grant digest binding.
claim_parent_tool_read(request_bytes: bytes) -> int: strict signed request + currentness/policy verification, unique allocation CAS, return accepted Ledger sequence only; performs no tool read.

record_parent_tool_observation(observation_bytes: bytes) -> int: verify accepted claim/purpose and actual inline raw/result bytes, append one immutable outcome. No reading the artifact path to reconstruct evidence.
read_parent_tool_operation(operation_id: str) -> immutable readback: concrete Ledger chain/row/signature/retained-byte verification; missing or unsettled state remains non-consumable. Never a permit.

issue_parent_tool_commit_ack(operation_id: str, phase: str, *, issuer_id: str, signer: Callable[[bytes],bytes]) -> bytes: authority-owned API, readback first, exact ACK-purpose identity required, verify signature after external signer. No worker-exposed signer/callback acceptance.

verify_parent_tool_commit_ack(ack_bytes: bytes, *, expected_request_bytes: bytes, expected_observation_bytes: bytes | None) -> immutable readback: strict purpose/phase/request/claim/retained-row join against self.ledger, not caller rows; no send/read authority.

Historical outcome after revocation does not become current/releasable. Old grants, new grant IDs or request UUIDs cannot refresh consumed allocation.
